snip.t: *Explanation:* This presentation is consistent with disseminated (miliary) tuberculosis, which can occur without prominent pulmonary findings on chest X-ray.
Asymptomatic state may cause miliary tuberculosis and TB meningitis.

qs.q: A patient with miliary tuberculosis undergoes a fundoscopic examination by an ophthalmologist. Which of the following specific findings might be visualized?
qs.e: Fundoscopy in miliary TB may show choroidal tubercles as a manifestation of blood-borne dissemination. Miliary TB itself presents with 2-3 weeks of fever, night sweats, and fine 1-2 mm lung lesions.

qs.q: Which of the following describes the radiographic appearance classically associated with miliary tuberculosis on a chest X-ray?
o: Unilateral pleural effusion with full opacification
Fine 1-2 mm lesions distributed across the lungs
A single massive cavitary lesion in the right lobe
qs.e: The classical appearances on chest X-ray for miliary TB are fine 1-2 mm lesions ('millet seed') distributed throughout the lung fields. Blood-borne dissemination gives rise to this presentation, sometimes accompanied by hepatosplenomegaly.
